facts.statement: Albert Burrer discovered the holotype specimen in the spring of 1909 in sediments from the Norian stage of the Triassic period.
facts.quote: The discovery was made by Albert Burrer in the spring of 1909 in white sandstone and gray/blue marl sediments that were deposited during the Norian stage of the Triassic period.

facts.statement: Eberhard Fraas named the genus Procompsognathus and the type species Procompsognathus triassicus in 1913.
facts.quote: Fraas in 1913 named the genus Procompsognathus with as type species, Procompsognathus triassicus.

facts.statement: Procompsognathus has usually been considered a theropod dinosaur, though some researchers have proposed alternative classifications.
facts.quote: It has since then usually been considered a theropod dinosaur, with some exceptions.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the holotype skull belongs to a theropod or a crocodylomorph, with Sankar Chatterjee arguing in 1993 that it is a theropod similar to Megapnosaurus.
facts.quote: However, in 1993 Sankar Chatterjee after further preparation refuted their assessment and regarded the skull as that of a theropod similar to Megapnosaurus, and demonstrated that it could not have been a crocodylomorph, as it lacks the landmark features of this group.

facts.statement: John Ostrom claimed in 1982 that specimens SMNS 12352 and SMNS 12352a belong to a taxon different from the holotype Procompsognathus.
facts.quote: In 1982 John Ostrom claimed that SMNS 12352 and SMNS 12352a originated from a taxon different from the holotype.

facts.statement: Fabien Knoll concluded in 2006 and 2008 that specimens SMNS 12352 and SMNS 12352a represent crocodylomorphs or other basal archosaurs, not Procompsognathus.
facts.quote: In 2006 and 2008 Fabien Knoll concluded that SMNS 12352 represented a crocodylomorph and SMNS 12352a a crocodylomorph or some other basal archosaur.

facts.statement: Procompsognathus is classified within the family Coelophysidae.
facts.quote: familia: Coelophysidae

facts.statement: Procompsognathus lived during the late Triassic Period, approximately 218 to 211 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 218 a 211 millones de años, en el Noriense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Procompsognathus was approximately 1.2 meters long, 26 centimeters high, and weighed about 1 kilogram.
facts.quote: Procompsognathus medía aproximadamente 1,2 metros de largo y 26 centímetros de alto, con un peso estimado de 1 kilogramo.

facts.statement: Procompsognathus had a long skull with elongated eye sockets.
facts.quote: Procompsognathus presentaba un largo cráneo con órbitas prolongadas.

facts.statement: This bipedal animal had long hind legs, short arms, hands with large claws, a thin long snout with many small teeth, and a stiff tail.
facts.quote: Este bípedo, tenía las piernas traseras largas, los brazos cortos, las manos con grandes garras, un hocico delgado y largo con muchos pequeños dientes, y una cola tiesa.

facts.statement: The tibia was about 20% longer than the femur in Procompsognathus, an adaptation correlated with cursorial habits, suggesting it was a good runner.
facts.quote: La tibia es aproximadamente un 20% más larga que el fémur en Procompsognathus , una adaptación que se ha correlacionado fuertemente con el desarrollo de hábitos cursoriales en los dinosaurios, lo que sugiere que eran buenos corredores.

facts.statement: It likely ate insects, lizards, and other small prey.
facts.quote: pudo haber comido insectos, lagartos y las otras pequeñas presas.

facts.statement: The discovery was made by Albert Burrer in spring 1909 in sediments deposited during the Norian stage of the Triassic period, approximately 210 million years ago.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento fue realizado por Albert Burrer en la primavera de 1909 en sedimentos de arenisca blanca y marga gris azulada que se depositaron durante la etapa noriana del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 210 millones de años.

facts.statement: Procompsognathus was named by Eberhard Fraas in 1913.
facts.quote: Procompsognathus fue nombrado por Eberhard Fraas en 1913.

facts.statement: He named the type species, P. triassicus, based on a poorly preserved skeleton from Württemberg, Germany.
facts.quote: Nombró a la especie tipo, P. triassicus, basándose en un esqueleto pobremente preservado de Württemberg, Alemania.

facts.statement: The holotype material of Procompsognathus was found in the Keuper Formation, Stubensandstein, Pfaffenhoffen, now Heilbron, Württemberg, Germany.
facts.quote: El material holotipo de Procompsognathus fue encontrado en al Formación Keuper, Stubensandstein, Pfaffenhoffen, hoy Heilbron, Wurttemberg. Alemania.

facts.statement: These remains cataloged as SMNS 12591 were described by Fraas in 1912 as Hallopus celerrimus and later in 1913 as Procompsognathus triassicus by the same author.
facts.quote: Estos restos catalogados como SMNS 12591, descrito por Frass en 1912 como Hallopus celerrimus y luego en 1913 como Procompsognathus triassicus por el mismo autor.

facts.statement: The skull was very fragmented but suggested a long narrow snout, a large anteorbital fossa, a large orbit, thin jaws with recurved teeth, a large infratemporal fenestra, and a narrower elliptical supratemporal fenestra.
facts.quote: El cráneo se encontraba muy fragmentado pero da la impresión de una forma larga y estrecha de hocico, con una fosa anteorbital grande, una órbita grande, quijadas delgadas con los dientes recurvados una ventana infratemporal grande, y una ventana supratemporal elíptica más estrecha.

facts.statement: The fragmentary and poorly preserved skeleton of Procompsognathus was found in the middle Stubensandstein member of the Löwenstein Formation at Weiße Steinbruch, Albert Burrer's quarry on the northern slopes of the Stromberg region near Pfaffenheim in Württemberg, Germany.
facts.quote: El esqueleto fragmentario y mal conservado de Procompsognathus se encontró en el miembro Stubensandstein medio de la Formación Löwenstein en Weiße Steinbruch, la cantera de Albert Burrer en las laderas norte de la región de Stromberg cerca de Pfaffenheim en Württemberg, Alemania.

facts.statement: The holotype SMNS 12591 consisted of three sandstone blocks: one showed a small skull, 7 centimeters long, severely flattened, with a lower jaw.
facts.quote: El holotipo SMNS 12591 constaba de tres bloques de arenisca: uno mostraba un cráneo pequeño, de 7 centímetros de largo, severamente aplastado, con mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: The second and third blocks contained partially articulated postcranial skeleton remains, including twenty-nine vertebrae of the neck, back, and tail; ribs, shoulder girdle elements, and a forelimb; an ilium, pubis, and hind legs.
facts.quote: El segundo y el tercero contenían los restos parcialmente articulados de un esqueleto poscraneal, que incluía veintinueve vértebras del cuello, la espalda y la cola; costillas elementos de la cintura escapular y una extremidad anterior; un ilion tanto el pubis como las patas traseras.

facts.statement: It represents an adult individual.
facts.quote: Representa a un individuo adulto.

facts.statement: In 1921, Friedrich von Huene referred two additional specimens, both found also at Burrer's quarry in 1908, to Procompsognathus: SMNS 12352, a partial skull and lower jaw of a larger individual than the holotype, and SMNS 12352a, an isolated left hand.
facts.quote: En 1921, Friedrich von Huene refirió dos especímenes más, ambos encontrados también en la cantera Burrer, en 1908, a Procompsognathus, SMNS 12352, un cráneo parcial y mandíbula inferior de un individuo más grande que el holotipo, y SMNS 12352a, una mano izquierda aislada.

facts.statement: However, in all comparable characters, the Welsh specimen is also very similar to Procompsognathus; further discoveries of additional material may demonstrate that the Welsh specimen can be referred to Procompsognathus.
facts.quote: No obstante en todos los caracteres que sean comparables, el espécimen galés es también muy similar a Procompsognathus; otros descubrimientos de materiales adicionales pueden demostrar que el espécimen de Gales puede ser referible a Procompsognathus.

facts.statement: Although it was undoubtedly a small carnivorous biped, the extremely poor preservation of the only known Procompsognathus fossil makes it difficult to determine its exact identity.
facts.quote: Aunque sin duda se trataba de un carnívoro pequeño y bípedo, la extremadamente pobre conservación del único fósil conocido de Procompsognathus hace que sea difícil de determinar su identidad exacta.

facts.statement: Fraas originally assigned it to Dinosauria.
facts.quote: Fraas lo asignó originalmente a los Dinosauria.

facts.statement: While historically cataloged as a theropod dinosaur, some experts consider Procompsognathus not as a dinosaur but as a primitive ornithodiran.
facts.quote: Si bien ha sido históricamente catalogado como un dinosaurio terópodo, algunos expertos consideran a Procompsognathus no como un dinosaurio, sino como un ornitodiro primitivo.

facts.statement: Sereno and Wild in 1992 considered the holotype specimen to be composed of two distinct animals.
facts.quote: Sereno y Wild en 1992 consideraron al espécimen holotipo como compuesto por dos distintos animales.

facts.statement: Sereno in 1997 and Ezcurra and Novas in 2007 performed phylogenetic analyses that supported the placement of Procompsognathus in the taxon Coelophysidae.
facts.quote: Sereno en 1997 y Ezcurra y Novas en 2007 realizaron análisis filogenéticos que respaldaron la ubicación de Procompsognathus en el taxón Coelophysidae.

facts.statement: In 1982, John Ostrom claimed that SMNS 12352 and SMNS 12352a originated from a taxon different from the holotype.
facts.quote: En 1982, John Ostrom afirmó que SMNS 12352 y SMNS 12352a se originaron a partir de un taxón diferente del holotipo.

facts.statement: In 2006 and 2008, Fabien Knoll concluded that SMNS 12352 represented a crocodylomorph and SMNS 12352a a crocodylomorph or some other basal archosaur.
facts.quote: En 2006 y 2008, Fabien Knoll concluyó que SMNS 12352 representaba un crocodilomorfo y SMNS 12352a un crocodilomorfo o algún otro arcosaurio basal.

facts.statement: In 2012, Knoll, after a computed tomography scan, reaffirmed that SMNS 12352 was a crocodylomorph but established that it was different from Saltoposuchus.
facts.quote: En 2012 Knoll después de una tomografía computarizada reafirmó que SMNS 12352 era un crocodilomorfo, pero estableció que era diferente de Saltoposuchus.

facts.statement: In 2004, David Allen considered Procompsognathus as a primitive non-dinosaurian ornithodiran.
facts.quote: En 2004 David Allen considera Procompsognathus como un primitivo ornithodiro no dinosauriano.

facts.quote: PBDB name: Procompsognathus (genus), Fraas 1913

facts.quote: Parent group: Coelophysidae

facts.quote: Type species: Procompsognathus triassicus

facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (215.38 to 211.18 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is currently only one recorded fossil occurrence of Procompsognathus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: In Michael Crichton's novels Jurassic Park and The Lost World, Procompsognathus appears as a genetically recreated species known as "compys".
facts.quote: En las novelas de Michael Crichton Jurassic Park y The Lost World, Procompsognathus, donde aparecen como "compys", es una de las especies recreadas por ingeniería genética.

facts.statement: In the novels, Procompsognathus is depicted as a scavenger and coprophage used to clean up sauropod feces.
facts.quote: Se los muestra como carroñeros y coprófagos, usados para limpiar el parque de los excrementos de los saurópodos.

facts.statement: While the author invented a venomous bite with soporific effects for Procompsognathus, there is no evidence to support venom in the animal.
facts.quote: Si bien el autor inventa una mordedura venenosa para Procompsognathus con efectos soporíferos , no hay evidencia que respalde el veneno en Procompsognathus.

facts.statement: In the second film adaptation, the character Robert Burke refers to them as Compsognathus triassicus, which is the type species of Procompsognathus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en la segunda película, Robert Burke se refiere a ellos como Compsognathus triassicus, triassicus es la especie tipo de Procompsognathus.
